original_value: A popular unsupervised learning method, known as clustering, is extensively used in data mining, machine learning and pattern recognition. The procedure involves grouping of single and distinct points in a group in such a way that they are either similar to each other or dissimilar to points of other clusters. Traditional clustering methods are greatly challenged by the recent massive growth of data. Therefore, several research works proposed novel designs for clustering methods that leverage the benefits of Big Data platforms, such as Apache Spark, which is designed for fast and distributed massive data processing. However, Spark-based clustering research is still in its early days. In this systematic survey, we investigate the existing Spark-based clustering methods in terms of their support to the characteristics Big Data. Moreover, we propose a new taxonomy for the Spark-based clustering methods. To the best of our knowledge, no survey has been conducted on Spark-based clustering of Big Data. Therefore, this survey aims to present a comprehensive summary of the previous studies in the field of Big Data clustering using Apache Spark during the span of 2010–2020. This survey also highlights the new research directions in the field of clustering massive data.

result.paraphrase: Clustering, a widely used unsupervised learning technique, is heavily applied in data mining, machine learning, and pattern recognition. It works by grouping individual distinct points into clusters so that members are similar to one another or dissimilar to points in other clusters. The recent explosive growth of data has put traditional clustering methods under great strain. As a result, many studies have introduced new clustering designs that take advantage of Big Data platforms such as Apache Spark, which is built for fast, distributed processing of massive data. Even so, Spark-based clustering research is still in its infancy. In this systematic survey, we examine existing Spark-based clustering methods according to how well they support Big Data characteristics. We also present a new taxonomy for Spark-based clustering approaches. To the best of our knowledge, no prior survey has addressed Spark-based clustering for Big Data. Accordingly, this survey provides a comprehensive overview of prior work in Big Data clustering with Apache Spark over the period 2010–2020 and points to new research directions for clustering massive data.
